课程简介（中文）

会计课程主要介绍会计的基本理论、基本方法和基本技能。课程内容包括导论、账户及复式记账、各种资产和负债的确认与计量、财务会计报告，以及财务报表的基本分析。

课程简介（英文）

The accounting course mainly introduces the fundamental theories, basic methods, and basic skills of accounting. It includes an introduction, accounts and double-entry bookkeeping, recognition and measurement of various assets and liabilities, financial accounting reporting, and basic analysis of financial statements.

教学目标

This introductory financial accounting course is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in understanding the fundamental principles, concepts, and practices of accounting. This course also aims to cultivate students’ awareness of integrity and professional ethics and enhance their sense of social responsibility. Through a combination of theoretical concepts and practical examples, students will develop the skills necessary to record, report, and understand transactions of business. The content and assessment standards of this course differ slightly from those of other parallel classes.

教学方式

Mainly focused on lectures, supplemented by group discussions to enhance students' understanding and participation

教学内容与进度安排

Week 1. Accounting in Business 1

  • Purpose of accounting
  • Users of accounting information
  • Ethics

Week 2. Accounting in Business 2

  • Accounting assumptions and accounting principles
  • Accounting equation and its use in business transactions analysis
  • Basic financial statements

Week 3. Analyzing and Recording Transactions 1

  • Steps in processing transactions
  • Source documents
  • Account and Ledger
  • Double-entry accounting

Week 4. Analyzing and Recording Transactions 2

  • Record transactions in a journal
  • Prepare and explain the use of a trial balance
  • Prepare financial statements from business transactions

Week 5. Adjusting Accounts for Financial Statements

  • Accrual accounting
  • Prepare and explain adjusting entries.
  • Explain and prepare an adjusted trial balance
  • Prepare financial statements from an adjusted trial balance
  • Understand the basic framework of corporate sustainability disclosure standards

Week 6.   Completing the Accounting Cycle

  • Temporary and permanent accounts
  • Classified balance sheet
  • Describe and prepare closing entries
  • Explain and prepare a post-closing trial balance
  • Tutorial 1

Week 7.  Accounting for Merchandising Operations

  • Merchandise activities and Income for merchandisers
  • Inventory asset, cost flows and inventory systems
  • Analyze and record transactions for merchandise purchases using a perpetual system
  • Analyze and record transactions for merchandise sales using a perpetual system
  • Quiz 1

Week 8. Inventories and cost of sales

  • Merchandise inventory items
  • Cost of merchandise inventory
  • Compute inventory in a perpetual system using the methods

Week 9. Cash

  • Basics of internal control
  • Cash and cash equivalents
  • Apply internal control to cash receipts and disbursements
  • Explain and record petty cash fund transactions
  • Prepare a bank reconciliation

Week 10. Receivables

  • Description of accounts receivable
  • Apply the direct write-off method to accounts receivable
  • Apply the allowance method to accounts receivable
  • Description of notes receivable

Week 11. Investment 

  • Description and classification of investments
  • Accounting basics for debts securities and equity securities
  • Account for trading securities
  • Account for held-to-maturity securities
  • Account for available-for-sales securities

Week 12. Plant Assets and Intangibles

  • Plant assets: recognition and cost determination
  • Depreciation
  • Capital expenditures and revenue expenditures
  • Account for asset disposal through discarding or selling an asset
  • Account for intangible assets
  • Recognition and measurement of data assets

Week 13. Tutorial 2 and Quiz 2

Week 14. Current Liabilities and Payroll Accounting

  • Description of liabilities
  • Known current liabilities
  • Prepare entries to account for short-term notes payable
  • Compute and record employee payroll deductions and liabilities

Week 15. Long-term Liabilities

  • Description of bonds
  • Prepare entries to record bond issuance and interest expense
  • Long-term notes payable
  • Introduction to new debt financing instruments such as Sci-Tech innovation bonds and green bonds

Week 16. Accounting for Corporations

  • Characteristics of corporations and their organization
  • Record the issuance of corporate stock
  • Record transactions involving cash dividends, stock dividends, and stock splits
  • Common and preferred stock
  • Tutorial 3

Week 17. Review

Week 18. Final Exam

This semester’s course is guided by An Introduction to Xi Jinping Thought on Economics, particularly the discussion on improving institutional mechanisms for developing new quality productive forces according to local conditions. Three frontier topics are integrated into the curriculum.

First, in Week 13: “Fixed Assets and Intangible Assets,” content on the recognition and measurement of data assets is added to reflect the policy direction of promoting market-oriented allocation of data elements and establishing systems for data property rights, transactions, and benefit protection, highlighting data as a new production factor in accounting.

Second, in Week 5: “Adjusting Entries and Financial Statement Preparation,” the course introduces Enterprise Sustainability Disclosure Standard No.1 — Climate (Trial) to respond to institutional requirements for green and low-carbon development and to enrich sustainability-related disclosures in financial reporting.

Third, in Week 15: “Long-term Liabilities,” technology innovation bonds and green bonds are introduced as examples of new financing instruments, reflecting policies that strengthen capital support for technological innovation and promote technology finance.

These adjustments better align the course with the development of new quality productive forces, helping students understand the market-oriented allocation of production factors, green transformation, and digital economy integration within the accounting framework.
